blocks.value: The Path class represents information about a file or directory (its location, whether it exists, and so on). The Files class performs actual operations on files and directories. Both come from the same package:
toAbsolutePath() converts a relative path into a full one based on the current working directory, so entering just "note.txt" might resolve to something like C:\Java\note.txt.

checkAccess() confirms a file exists and, optionally, whether the program has permission to READ, WRITE, or EXECUTE it. delete() removes a file or directory, throwing an exception if it can't (for example NoSuchFileException if the file isn't there); deleteIfExists() does the same without throwing an exception when the file simply doesn't exist.
readAttributes() retrieves details about a file, like its size, creation time, and last modified time, returned as a BasicFileAttributes object.
